new_packages.label: חוֹלָם וְהַמְתָּקָה
new_packages.reason: The vowel cholam, the three divine YHVH names, sweetening (hamtaka), pidyon nefesh, and the verse 'v'rapo y'rapei' all share the same essential nature: they are the mechanism of sweetening harsh judgment. The Rebbe explicitly uses bechina and gematria language to equate them. Cholam = gematria of three YHVH names; the three YHVH names sweeten the three Elokim; 'v'rapo y'rapei' = gematria of pidyon nefesh. These are all parallel expressions of the redemptive sweetening.

observations: Torah #3 of LM2 is a short, tightly focused teaching about the relationship between pidyon (spiritual redemption/ransom) and physical healing. The main body (lines 1-8) is a purely causal argument: pidyon sweetens judgment, which opens the window for the doctor to heal — these are all eitza relationships and were correctly captured in the dataset as such. The final section (lines 9-10) shifts into Kabbalistic bechina language, mapping the Torah's argument onto the vowel system: cholam = sweetening (the first step), tzeirei = healing (the second step). This creates a beautiful structural parallel: the word 'v'rapo' (cholam) is the hamtaka step, and 'y'rapei' (tzeirei) is the refuah step — the same two-phase argument encoded in the vowels of a single verse. The dataset currently lacks ALL of these bechina relationships. Once added, two clean packages would emerge: (1) Cholam/Sweetening/Pidyon and (2) Tzeirei/Healing/Refuot, with a potential evil mirror in the Elokim/Katnut cluster that represents the judgment being sweetened. The two good packages relate to each other via eitza: Package 1 (sweetening) ENABLES Package 2 (healing) — exactly mirroring the Torah's core argument. This Torah also exhibits no good/evil mirror in the classical sense (evil package mirroring good) — the teaching is almost entirely about the positive process. The 'negative' element (din/judgment/katnut) is presented as the obstacle being overcome, not as an independent evil domain with its own internal bechina structure.
